issues.description: The template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java is structurally incorrect and does not match the problem specification or the solution: the file declares a class named AnimalFarm (not Farm), contains a duplicated 'package' and 'class' declaration nested inside a method, and does not provide the expected 'animals' List attribute or the correct method stubs/signatures. This malformed file will cause compile errors and prevents students from implementing the intended design (a Farm class with a List<Animal>, constructor, getters/setters, addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, and singFarmSong).
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the malformed template file with a correctly structured Farm.java: declare 'public class Farm' (matching the filename), add 'private List<Animal> animals;', provide a no-arg constructor that initializes 'animals' to a new ArrayList<>() , and include the expected public methods (getAnimals, setAnimals, addAnimal(Animal), feedAllAnimals(), singFarmSong()) and a private helper singFarmSongVerse(Animal). Remove duplicate/nested 'package' or 'class' declarations so the file compiles and matches the UML in the problem statement.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a class named 'Farm' (the central entity holding the animals and providing methods like addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, singFarmSong). In the template repository the corresponding file Farm.java defines a class named 'AnimalFarm' instead. This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual entity will confuse students mapping the requirements to the starter code, can cause compilation/name-resolution issues, and forces students to reconcile two different names for the same concept.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class in the template file to 'Farm' (class Farm) to match the problem statement and solution. Ensure the public class name matches the filename Farm.java and update any references in the template Main or other starter files accordingly.
